question.text: Why must even careful drivers know what to do after a crash, and what should ride in the car?

answer.text: Over three hundred thousand state crashes yearly strike even careful lawful drivers through surprises and others mistakes, so crash parties must act responsibly on scene and obey reporting law, with flares and first-aid kits from department or auto stores riding aboard.

teaching.text: Crashes happen even to careful, lawful drivers, so carry flares and a first-aid kit and know your duties at the scene. Remember: flares and first aid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Over three hundred thousand state crashes yearly strike even careful lawful drivers through surprises and others mistakes, so crash parties must act responsibly on scene and obey reporting law, with flares and first-aid kits from department or auto stores riding aboard.

question.text: Must you stop after every crash, and what is it called if you leave?

answer.text: Every crash demands a stop whatever the damage, flight from property-only scenes counts as a traffic violation, and flight from fatal or injury scenes counts as criminal.

teaching.text: Stop after every crash, whatever the damage; leaving is a violation or, with injuries, a crime. Remember: always stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every crash demands a stop whatever the damage, flight from property-only scenes counts as a traffic violation, and flight from fatal or injury scenes counts as criminal.

question.text: How does leaving a property-only crash differ from leaving an injury or fatal crash?

answer.text: Fleeing property-only scenes breaks traffic law while fleeing injury or fatal scenes breaks criminal law, one stop with two flight crimes.

teaching.text: One duty to stop, two kinds of flight: property-only is a traffic violation, injury or fatal is criminal. Remember: traffic versus criminal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fleeing property-only scenes breaks traffic law while fleeing injury or fatal scenes breaks criminal law, one stop with two flight crimes.

question.text: What information must drivers exchange after a property-only crash?

answer.text: Property-only crashes still force exchanges of name address license registration and insurance including policy number and effective date with fellow drivers and scene police, plus insurance cards shown on demand.

teaching.text: Even with only property damage, swap name, address, license, registration and insurance details, including the policy number and effective date. Remember: swap the details.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Property-only crashes still force exchanges of name address license registration and insurance including policy number and effective date with fellow drivers and scene police, plus insurance cards shown on demand.

question.text: What must you do if you damage a parked vehicle, other property or a domestic animal?

answer.text: Harm to parked vehicles non-vehicle property or domestic animals obliges finding owners or notifying police.

teaching.text: If you damage a parked vehicle, other property or a domestic animal, find the owner or tell the police. Remember: find the owner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Harm to parked vehicles non-vehicle property or domestic animals obliges finding owners or notifying police.

question.text: What must you do at once if anyone is hurt or killed?

answer.text: Any injury or death summons police at once with ambulance or rescue confirmed en route.

teaching.text: If anyone is hurt or killed, call the police at once and make sure an ambulance or rescue is coming. Remember: call police, ambulance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any injury or death summons police at once with ambulance or rescue confirmed en route.

question.text: How do you make a crash scene safer?

answer.text: Vehicles clear the roadway when able while reflectors or flares guard scenes against leaking fuel and live traffic for everybody present.

teaching.text: Move vehicles off the road if you can, and use reflectors or flares to protect everyone from leaking fuel and traffic. Remember: clear and guard.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles clear the roadway when able while reflectors or flares guard scenes against leaking fuel and live traffic for everybody present.

question.text: What should drivers not involved in a crash do?

answer.text: Uninvolved drivers roll past unless aid lags, eyes on driving and officer orders.

teaching.text: If you were not involved, keep driving past unless help has not arrived, and watch the road and any officer. Remember: keep driving past.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Uninvolved drivers roll past unless aid lags, eyes on driving and officer orders.

question.text: When may you move an injured person, and how?

answer.text: Injured people stay put short of fire or mortal peril, and forced moves brace backs and necks straight with arms beneath torsos and upper arms cradling necks while gripped clothes drag victims head-first clear.

teaching.text: Leave an injured person still unless fire or deadly danger forces a move, then keep the back and neck straight. Remember: move only if danger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Injured people stay put short of fire or mortal peril, and forced moves brace backs and necks straight with arms beneath torsos and upper arms cradling necks while gripped clothes drag victims head-first clear.

question.text: When do injured people stay put, and when may they be moved?

answer.text: Injured bodies stay untouched through ordinary scenes yet move under fire or mortal threat with braced straight spines dragged head-first clear.

teaching.text: Stay put is the rule; a move is only for fire or deadly danger, dragging head-first with the spine straight. Remember: still unless threatened.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Injured bodies stay untouched through ordinary scenes yet move under fire or mortal threat with braced straight spines dragged head-first clear.

question.text: What should you do about downed wires at a crash?

answer.text: Downed wires repel approach, and wire-touched vehicles hold occupants inside until rescuers come.

teaching.text: Keep away from downed wires, and if wires touch your car, stay inside until rescuers arrive. Remember: stay away, stay inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Downed wires repel approach, and wire-touched vehicles hold occupants inside until rescuers come.

question.text: What do rescuers and occupants each do when wires are down?

answer.text: Fallen wires keep rescuers back while wire-touched cars keep riders inside, patience both ways until crews arrive.

teaching.text: With wires down, everyone waits: rescuers stay back and occupants stay in. Remember: patience both ways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fallen wires keep rescuers back while wire-touched cars keep riders inside, patience both ways until crews arrive.

question.text: Which crashes must be reported to the motor-vehicle agency?

answer.text: Fatal injury or one-thousand-dollar-plus single-victim property crashes demand motor-vehicle reports on crash forms stocked at offices agents and the agency website.

teaching.text: Injury and fatal crashes, and property crashes above the damage threshold for one victim, need a motor-vehicle report. Remember: injury or large damage.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fatal injury or one-thousand-dollar-plus single-victim property crashes demand motor-vehicle reports on crash forms stocked at offices agents and the agency website.

question.text: How do the reporting triggers for injuries differ from those for property damage?

answer.text: Deaths and injuries always report while property reports only past one thousand dollars to a single victim, harm-based versus threshold triggers.

teaching.text: Injuries and deaths always trigger a report; property damage triggers one only above the threshold. Remember: harm versus threshold.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Deaths and injuries always report while property reports only past one thousand dollars to a single victim, harm-based versus threshold triggers.

question.text: When must the crash report be filed, and is telling your insurer enough?

answer.text: Insurer notice never satisfies law since motor-vehicle filings land within ten days under misdemeanor peril suspending or revoking driver and owner credentials, and hurt drivers cede filing to passengers or owners.

teaching.text: File the motor-vehicle report within ten days; telling your insurer does not count, and missing it risks your license. Remember: ten days, not insurer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Insurer notice never satisfies law since motor-vehicle filings land within ten days under misdemeanor peril suspending or revoking driver and owner credentials, and hurt drivers cede filing to passengers or owners.

question.text: Why does calling your insurer not meet the reporting requirement?

answer.text: Calling insurers starts claims but never files law, since motor-vehicle reports still land within ten days under misdemeanor and credential peril.

teaching.text: An insurance call starts a claim, but only the motor-vehicle report meets the law. Remember: claims are not reports.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Calling insurers starts claims but never files law, since motor-vehicle reports still land within ten days under misdemeanor and credential peril.

hooks_spoken: Stop after every crash; leaving a property-only scene is a traffic violation, leaving an injury scene is a crime.
Exchange name, address, license, registration and insurance, and call police at once for any injury.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of stopping and exchanging information. Stop after every crash; leaving a property-only scene is a traffic violation, leaving an injury scene is a crime. Exchange name, address, license, registration and insurance, and call police at once for any injury. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Leave injured people where they are unless fire or deadly danger forces a move, and stay away from downed wires.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of keeping a crash scene safe. Leave injured people where they are unless fire or deadly danger forces a move, and stay away from downed wires. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Report injury and fatal crashes and larger property crashes to the motor-vehicle agency within ten days, even if you told your insurer.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of reporting a crash. Report injury and fatal crashes and larger property crashes to the motor-vehicle agency within ten days, even if you told your insurer. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
